newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PENPIX OF BRAZIL SQUAD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PENPIX OF BRAZIL SQUAD.

text.p: Pen pictures of the Brazil squad for Sunday's Copa America quarter-final against Paraguay.
Goalkeepers

Taffarel (Claudio Andre Mergen Taffarel). Atletico Mineiro. 30. Brazil's regular goalkeeper from 1988 to 1995, including the last two World Cups. He stepped down after criticism of his performance in the 1995 Copa America, vowing not to play again, but was recalled earlier this year after a re-think.
Carlos Germano. (Carlos Germano Schwambach). Vasco da Gama. 26. Has played in a handful of friendlies but never in a major international tournament.
Defenders

Aldair. (Aldair Nascimento Santos). Roma, Italy. 31. Called in at the last minute for the 1994 World Cup after the three first-choice defenders were forced out through injury, he has played in every game ever since. Played in the Atlanta Olympics as an over-age player.
Cafu. (Marcos Evangelista de Moraes). Palmeiras. 26. Has taken over from Jorginho as automatic choice at right-back.
Celio Silva. (Vagno Celio da Nascimento Silva). Corinthians. 29. He has played in a smattering of friendlies since 1992. Possesses one of the most powerful shots in the game.

Goncalves. (Marcelo Goncalves Costa Lopes). Botafogo. 31. A latecomer to the international scene, a five-year spell in Mexican soccer possibly keeping him out of the view of the national team coach. Inspired Botafogo as they won the Brazilian championship in 1995.

Marcio Santos. (Marcio Roberto dos Santos). Atletico Mineiro. 27. Made his mark at the 1994 World Cup after injuries to three other defenders gave him a chance. A troubled spell at Dutch club Ajax led to a loss of form. Recalled for April's friendly with Mexico.

Roberto Carlos. (Roberto Carlos da Silva). Real Madrid, Spain. 24. Fast and powerful left-back with a thunderous shot. Played in the last two Copa America tournaments and the Atlanta Olympics but was controversially left out of the 1994 World Cup squad.
Ze Maria. (Jose Marcelo Ferreira). Real Madrid, Spain. 23. Surprise choice as Cafu's reserve. Many thought Vasco defender Pimentel deserved the place. Played in the Atlanta Games last year.
Midfielders

Cesar Sampaio. (Carlos Cesar Sampaio Campos). Yokohama Flugels, Japan. 29. Defensive midfielder who played in the 1993 and 1995 Copa America tournaments but was overlooked for the last World Cup. His recall for last month's friendly against Mexico ended a two-year absence from the national team.
Denilson. (Denilson de Oliveira). Sao Paulo. 19. Pacey, left-sided player of enormous promise.

Djalminha. (Djalma Feitosa Dias). Palmeiras. 26. Hugely gifted left-footed player who is seen as the potential playmaker if he can keep his temper under control. He has been sent off three times this year in club matches and was once thrown out of Flamengo for coming to blows with a teammate during a game. His father Djalma Dias was a Brazil international.
Dunga. (Carlos Caetano Verri). Jubilo Iwata, Japan. 33. Gritty midfielder who captained the 1994 World Cup team. Surprisingly recalled this year after an 18-month absence.
Flavio Conceicao. (Flavio da Conceicao). Deportivo Coruna, Spain. 22. Made his name with Palmeiras. Played at the Atlanta Olympics.

Giovanni. (Giovanni Silva de Oliveira). Barcelona, Spain. 25. Elegant player who made his name with Santos. Fighting Djalminha and Juninho, who was left out of the squad, for the main midfield role. Inconsistency and problems at his club, where he has been subjected to spells on the substitutes' bench, have affected his international form.

Leonardo. (Leonardo de Araujo). Paris St Germain, France. 27. Began his career as a left-back but is now established as an attacking midfielder. Played in the 1994 World Cup until he was sent off in the second round for elbowing an opponent and suspended from the rest of the competition.

Mauro Silva. (Mauro da Silva). Deportivo Coruna, Spain. 29. Good distribution combined with solid marking have made him a regular in front of the defence since his debut in 1991. Has yet to score for his country.
Ze Roberto. (Jose Roberto da Silva Junior). Real Madrid, Spain. 22. Can switch from full-back to an attacking midfield role. Raised at Portuguesa.
Forwards

Edmundo. (Edmundo Alves de Souza Neto). Vasco da Gama. 26. Hugely talented and hugely temperamental player. Can tantalise opponents with his dribbling and his coaches with his attitude. Sent off three times this year in club games and frequently gets into blazing rows with teammates and opponents alike.

Paulo Nunes. (Arilson de Paulo Nunes). Gremio. 25. Tricky, talented striker whose call-up was a reward after helping his club win the South American Libertadores Cup in 1995 and the Brazilian championship last year.

Romario. (Romario de Souza Faria). Flamengo. 31. Brazil's hero at the last World Cup with five goals, he has scored 26 times in his 42 full games. Disciplinary problems have led to him being left out of the team for long spells. Made his comeback this year after a two-year absence imposed by coach Mario Zagallo for lack of enthusiasm. Has scored five goals in his last two games.

Ronaldo (Ronaldo Luis Nazario de Lima). Barcelona, Spain. 20. Widely considered the world's best player. Included in the 1994 World Cup squad at the age of 17, although he did not get a game. Has scored 12 goals in his 18 appearances.
